title: Slice pullback comparison is induced by the ringed localization square
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a continuous functor defining a morphism $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ whose inverse image preserves finite limits, and let $R$ on $\mathcal D$ and $S$ on $\mathcal C$ be sheaves of commutative rings with a ring map $c:f^{-1}R\to S$. For $V\in\mathcal D$ put $U=u(V)$, give $\mathcal D/V$ and $\mathcal C/U$ the localized topologies and restricted rings [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and let $f_V$, the commutative ringed localization square and the ordinary module comparison $\sigma:(f_V)^*j_V^*\cong j_U^*f^*$ be those of [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. Use the unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with localization functor $q$, the exact derived restrictions $j_V^*,j_U^*$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction], the derived pullbacks $Lf^*,Lf_V^*$ computed on K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], and the derived adjunctions $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Lf_V^*\dashv R(f_V)_*$. Let $\beta:j_V^*Rf_*\cong R(f_V)_*j_U^*$ and $\theta:Lf_V^*j_V^*\cong j_U^*Lf^*$ be the canonical comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization]. Then for every K-flat complex $P$ of $R$-modules with flat terms, under the identifications $Lf^*(qP)\cong q(f^*P)$ and $Lf_V^*(q\,j_V^*P)\cong q((f_V)^*j_V^*P)$ (the restriction $j_V^*P$ is again K-flat with flat terms) and the termwise identifications $j_V^*(qP)=q(j_V^*P)$, $j_U^*(q f^*P)=q(j_U^*f^*P)$, the component $\theta_{qP}$ equals $q(\sigma_P)$. Consequently $\theta$ is the derived pullback comparison induced by the commutative ringed localization square, and $\beta$ is its exchange mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], that is, the base change map of this square.

proof.text:
Write $F=f^*$, $G=f_*$, $F_v=(f_V)^*$, $G_v=(f_V)_*$ on complexes and $r=j_V^*$, $s=j_U^*$ for restrictions. In this proof $a;b$ means first $a$, then $b$. The localization theorem supplies the localized continuous morphism and its ring map, with no assumption that $f$ is flat. Let $\tau_I:rGI\to G_vsI$ be the ordinary direct-image comparison. By [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] it is identity on sections with the restricted scalar action. The ordinary inverse-mate assertion [lem-weil-pbc-slice-module-pullback-isIso] identifies the ordinary comparison $\sigma_P:F_vrP\to sFP$ by
$$\mathsf T'_0(\sigma_P)=r(\eta^0_P);\tau_{FP},$$
where $\mathsf T'_0$ is the local ordinary adjunction bijection and $\eta^0$ the global ordinary unit. Applied degreewise this is the same identity for complexes: naturality of all components with the differential makes the displayed arrows chain maps.

source.place: Tag 04J0 (sites-modules.tex, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites), ordinary localization square and its adjoint normalization

proof.text:
Put $L=Lf^*$, $R=Rf_*$, $L_v=Lf_V^*$ and $R_v=R(f_V)_*$. Use the normalized presentations supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-image-exists]: write $\alpha_A:LqA\to qFA$, $\iota_I:qGI\to RqI$, and $\alpha',\iota'$ for their local counterparts. With $\mathsf T_D,\mathsf T_0$ the global derived and ordinary Hom bijections, their normalization is
$$\mathsf T_D(\alpha_A;q h)=q(\mathsf T_0(h));\iota_I\quad(h:FA\to I),$$
and similarly locally. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-comparisons], the canonical $\beta$ satisfies, for every complex $I$,
$$r(\iota_I);\beta_{qI}=q(\tau_I);\iota'_{sI}.$$
Here and below all termwise restriction factorizations are inserted: $rqA\cong q(rA)$ and $sqI\cong q(sI)$ are the canonical identifications of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]; these identifications are natural in chain maps. The $\beta$ and inverse mate in this normalized presentation are the canonical comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization]. Its pullback comparison in the orientation of the item is $\theta:L_vr\to sL$ (the inverse of the comparison written in the opposite orientation there).

proof.text: Apply the K-flat preservation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the localization morphism $j_V$ with identity coefficient map. Its ordinary pullback is restriction, so $rP$ is K-flat with flat terms whenever $P$ is. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], $\alpha_P$ and $\alpha'_{rP}$ are isomorphisms. Exact derived restrictions have the termwise factorizations of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction], so these are precisely the two K-flat identifications specified in the item. In the remaining calculation we keep the comparison arrows visible rather than replace them by identities.

proof.text:
Let $\eta^D,\eta'^D$ be the global and local derived units. Specializing Step 2's global normalized Hom identity to $h=1_{FP}$ gives
$$\eta^D_{qP};R(\alpha_P)=q(\eta^0_P);\iota_{FP},$$
since the adjunct of an identity is the unit. Compatibility with units in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization] gives
$$\eta'^D_{rqP};R_v(\theta_{qP})=r(\eta^D_{qP});\beta_{LqP}.$$
Indeed its unit equation with $\theta^{-1}$ becomes this equation after composing with $R_v(\theta)$ and cancelling the inverse. No invertibility of a right-derived augmentation is needed.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), units and normalization; mate unit identity

proof.text:
Compute the local derived transpose of $a=\theta_{qP};s(\alpha_P)$, with target $sqFP=q(sFP)$. By the unit formula for the adjunction bijection, Step 4 and naturality of $\beta$ at $\alpha_P$, it is
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathsf T'_D(a)
&=r(\eta^D_{qP});\beta_{LqP};R_v(s(\alpha_P))\\
&=r(\eta^D_{qP};R(\alpha_P));\beta_{qFP}\\
&=q(r(\eta^0_P));r(\iota_{FP});\beta_{qFP}\\
&=q(r(\eta^0_P);\tau_{FP});\iota'_{sFP}.
\end{aligned}$$
The third equality substitutes Step 4's normalized global unit. The last substitutes the normalized right square of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-comparisons] at the actual complex $I=FP$. Naturality of the restriction factorizations in Step 2 gives the displayed $q(r(\eta^0_P))$; thus the computation is also valid with all those canonical isomorphisms inserted. The complex $FP$ need not be K-injective.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), explicit unit/naturality calculation with Tag 04J0 direct-image normalization

proof.text:
For $b=\alpha'_{rP};q(\sigma_P)$, the local normalized Hom identity of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-image-exists], applied to the chain map $\sigma_P:F_vrP\to sFP$, and Step 1 give
$$\mathsf T'_D(b)=q(\mathsf T'_0(\sigma_P));\iota'_{sFP}
=q(r(\eta^0_P);\tau_{FP});\iota'_{sFP}.$$
This equals Step 5. Injectivity of the local adjunction bijection proves
$$\theta_{qP};s(\alpha_P)=\alpha'_{rP};q(\sigma_P).$$
Cancel the two model isomorphisms of Step 3 to obtain exactly $\theta_{qP}=q(\sigma_P)$ under the identifications in the statement. This is equality of the specified maps; it does not merely show that both are invertible.

source.place: Tags 07A6 and 04J0; normalized transpose calculation on flat-term K-flat models

proof.text:
Every derived object has a flat-term K-flat representative by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Explicitly, for a complex $A$ choose a quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to A$ of that kind. Its image $qp$ is invertible, and naturality forces
$$\theta_{qA}=L_vr(qp)^{-1};\theta_{qP};sL(qp).$$
Thus the model equality just proved determines $\theta$ on all objects and is independent of the chosen resolution. It is the pullback comparison induced by the ordinary ringed localization square. The counit compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization] says
$$L_v(\beta_M);\varepsilon'_{sM}=\theta_{RM};s(\varepsilon_M).$$
By the defining mate bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], this says precisely that $\beta_M$ is the transpose of $\theta_{RM};s(\varepsilon_M)$. Stacks 07A7 defines the base change map of this ringed square as that transpose, proving the final identification.

split_report.summary: Proved the representative equality by a normalized adjunction-unit calculation, using existing ordinary inverse-mate, derived normalization and K-flat preservation statements. No new nodes and no changes to the statement. Kept all restriction factorization and K-flat comparison arrows explicit up to the stated canonical identifications; derived base change is identified by its counit transpose.

tool_uses.why: Used solely to choose a flat-term K-flat representative for an arbitrary module-sheaf complex, for independence and determination of the derived comparison. This general resolution existence theorem is not a replacement of the proper-base-change unit route and no node of this unit gives the more general existence statement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q02-eaf152205 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all 7 steps and checked every cited statement, including the Lean statements: RingedSliceDerivedImage.normalized at RingedDerivedSliceData.lean l.118, the RingedSliceAdjunctionSquare unit and counit fields, the right-derived-unit square in ringedDerivedSliceComparisons and in ringedDerivedSliceLocalization, and the lambda adjunct formula in localize_ringed_site_morphism_general. Step 1: sigma is pinned by T'_0(sigma_P)=r(eta^0_P);tau_FP, which matches the slice-module-pullback-isIso formula. Steps 4-6: I recomputed the transpose of theta;s(alpha) through beta naturality, the normalized global unit and the right square at I=FP, and it equals the local normalization at sigma_P. Injectivity then gives theta_qP=q(sigma_P) after cancelling alpha and alpha', which are K-flat isomorphisms (restriction keeps K-flat flat-term complexes K-flat by the tensor-pullback clause applied to j_V with the identity ring map). Step 7: the counit field plus the def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate transpose shows beta is the mate of theta, which is the Stacks 07A7 base change map (sites-cohomology l.4033, square g=j_V, f'=f_V, g'=j_U); the 04J0 square in sites-modules l.2369 also matches. Edge cases checked: singleton sites, a non-flat A->A/(a), unbounded complexes. No new nodes, no duplicate of the item in the DAG, no SGA. Accepted tool use: lem-pc-kflat-resolution, which is generic resolution existence. Maintainer notes, not faults of this delivery: slice-module-pullback-isIso writes its orientations garbled in words; the word statement of ringed-derived-slice-localization does not name the right-derived-unit square that pins beta (only its Lean statement does); step 1's source.document is sites-cohomology although its place correctly names sites-modules 04J0.
